newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan budget one step from final approval.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan budget one step from final approval.

text.p: The lower house of Venezuela's Congress approved the government's 7.8 trillion bolivar ($16.6 billion) 1997 budget proposal for the second time Wednesday, legislators said.
Approval in the Chamber of Deputies means the bill only requires the go-ahead from the Senate to gain final approval. The Senate vote is expected to take place Thursday.
The bill was passed with the votes of opposition union-based Radical Cause, social Christian Copei and government-backing Movement to Socialism (MAS) parties.

Leading opposition party social democratic Democratic Action (AD) abstained in disagreement over spending reallocations made to the original budget proposal. The left-leaning government Convergence party also abstained from several clauses of the bill in disagreement over the spending reallocations.
Congressmen said a motion will be presented in the Senate to give the bill constitutional urgency -- a move which would allow it to be approved after one hearing instead of the usual two.
The budget proposal must be approved before ordinary sessions end at the end of the month to prevent a roll-over budget based on spending in 1996.
